findings: Sixteen independently owned whole triangle executors replace the four-entry cache. Eviction still precedes successor construction; compiled models and infer requests are not shared.

Only four exact captured compositor shaders use 8192-lane pixel graphs on the pinned runtime. Other programs retain a 4096 preferred raster size; legacy arithmetic remains bounded to 512 for those compositor shaders. Existing arithmetic ceilings still apply.

The renderer passes its preferred capacity explicitly to the provider-independent transport scheduler. The standalone packet helper retains its original library dependencies. Protocol ABI and bytes are unchanged.

Two historical full draws pass repeated CPU and NPU execution with exact historical output hashes and scalar-checked coverage. The partial point capture, full-partial-full worker transition, sixty DDI draws and eight clears remain valid.

The actual candidate worker preserves all seventeen prewarm images and all sixty-three mixed captured packet images and coverage. Provider request and tile counts may decrease with the larger batches; those differences are recorded explicitly.

Both runtimes pass fresh builds and all twenty-five CPU suites. Native NPU qualification supports an installed VM experiment; it does not establish a usable full desktop, physical scanout offload or Tahoma improvement.

The first mixed-packet run takes 95.257 seconds; an identical-order repeat takes 37.73 seconds, with exact pixels and coverage again. The first-run setup penalty is consistent with warming newly shaped models, but this worker does not record per-request compilation counters, so compilation is not isolated as its sole cause. This qualification is not a controlled desktop-performance comparison.
